contentHtml:
WoW: Forever's beta level cap is now raised to 30, and everyone wants to try it - so we're helping with that opportunity! We're giving away even more Skyborne Epic Packs in our latest sweepstakes.

This time, there are 45 Skyborne Epic Packs up for grabs, which lets even more people try out WoW: Forever during the last stretch of beta and beyond!



To enter for a chance to win, simply comment below on this article with what class you'll get to level 30 first in WoW: Forever! The official release date for Forever is November 4th, but from now until October 21st, players can test out the Beta and see what's in store on official release.

45 total winners will be selected and contacted by Monday, October 12th. Good luck!





The Prizes
Grand Prize (x45):
Everyone is a Grand Prize winner in this sweepstakes, and with 45 Skyborne Epic Packs to go out, each winner will receive access to the WoW: Forever beta until its conclusion on October 21, in-game goodies like mounts, transmog, and toys, early name reservation for Forever's launch, 30 days of WoW game time, housing decor, and of course, unlock the new Skyborne race!
  • Winners will be selected by random drawing from all eligible entries received.
  • One (1) entry per person, regardless of entry method. Multiple comments or entries will not increase your odds of winning.
  • The Sweepstakes begins at the publishing of this post on October 7th, 2026 and ends at 11:59:59 PM PT on October 11th, 2026. Entries received outside the Sweepstakes Period will not be eligible.
  • To enter through this article, your entry must be submitted in the comment section below and contain a valid response. Comments on other Wowhead posts or social media will not count as entries.
  • Comments removed for spam or violations of Wowhead's site rules will not be eligible for entry and may be subject to normal site moderation.
  • Potential winners will be contacted by October 12th, 2026 and will have three (3) days to respond and satisfy the applicable eligibility requirements.
  • Winners may need to confirm their age, location, and eligibility before receiving a prize. Anyone who is ineligible or can't legally receive a prize will be disqualified, and a new winner will be randomly drawn.
  • Legal Disclaimers, Eligibility Addendum and Official Rules

title.en: Rogue and Warlock Class Deep Dive in World of Warcraft: Forever
title.es: Profunda inmersión de clase pícaro y brujo en World of Warcraft: Forever

summary.en: Rogue and Warlock Class Deep Dive in World of Warcraft: Forever...
summary.es: Profunda inmersión de clase Pícaro y Brujo en World of Warcraft: Forever...

contentHtml:
Blizzard has posted a class deep dive for Rogues and Warlocks in WoW: Forever.
Blizzard
View Original
Masters of subtlety and destructive power take center stage in this World of Warcraft: Forever class deep dive. Discover how Rogues and Warlocks are evolving through updates that build on the defining tools, tactics, and playstyles of each class.

For Rogues, the update builds on their mastery of Stealth, control, Poisons, and precise weapon attacks. Poisons gain more charges and can be used alongside temporary weapon enchantments, while updates across Assassination, Combat, and Subtlety create stronger options for daggers, other weapon types, Finishing Moves, Bleeds, and combat tricks.

For Warlocks, the focus is on opening new ways to command Shadow, Fire, and demonic power. Banes separate damaging effects from utility Curses, pets scale with their master’s stats, and revised Firestones and Spellstones strengthen spell-focused weapon imbues. Talent updates across Affliction, Demonology, and Destruction further support damage-over-time and draining effects, deeper demon synergies, and distinct Shadow and Fire combinations.

Talents become available starting at level 10 and continue using a familiar structure, including one-point milestone talents at 11, 21, and 31 points, now joined by a new 16-point milestone. To change your talents, including Legacy talents, visit a class trainer in one of the major cities. Dual Specialization also becomes available at level 40.

Please note that class abilities and talents may continue to evolve throughout the beta test and are subject to additional changes.
  • Rogue
  • Warlock

Rogue: Every Advantage Counts


Rogues excel at creating opportunities and turning them into decisive advantages. These updates give them more ways to prepare for an encounter, adapt once combat begins, and shape a build around the methods that suit them best.

Baseline Abilities

  • Poisons
    • Charges increased on all poisons.
    • Poisons can now be applied to weapons at the same time as temporary enchantments like Weightstones and Sharpening Stones.
  • Feint: Threat reduction doubled.
  • Sap: Using this ability no longer breaks Stealth.
    We want Rogues to have a crowd control benefit they can provide to parties and raids that requires their unique skills to set up (Stealth, Distract, etc.) but which can be used tactically when there are too many monsters in a group to be safely tanked.
  • Distract: This ability now also causes affected enemies to have reduced Stealth detection for 10 seconds. However, this debuff also means player enemies will now know there is a Rogue nearby to look for.
  • Expose Armor: Armor reduction increased to match the armor reduction caused by 5 applications of Sunder Armor at approximately the same level.
    Expose Armor no longer prevents Sunder Armor from being used on a target, but Sunder Armor will still not overwrite Expose Armor, unless its effect is weaker. This allows Warriors to generate threat from Sunder Armor without Expose Armor interfering.
  • Axes: Rogues can now learn to equip one-handed axes. This increase in itemization choices lets us make a more diverse offering of weapons and know that Rogues will still benefit. Rogues as an archetype include brigands and outlaws, who often make use of axes in fantasy and medieval storytelling.

Talents

Assassination

  • Improved Gouge: Moved to row 1 of Assassination from Combat.
  • Remorseless Attacks: Now also affects Mutilate.
  • Malice: Now increases your critical strike chance with all attacks and Poisons, instead of just melee attacks.
  • Murder: Now also applies to Giants but no longer applies to Beasts and Dragonkin.
  • Improved Expose Armor: (Redesigned.) No longer increases the effectiveness of Expose Armor, instead reduces the Energy cost of Expose Armor and Expose Armor now refunds Combo Points when used with 5 Combo Points.
  • Lethality: Now also applies to Mutilate. Bonus to critical damage also lowered some.
  • Cold Blood: Moved from 21-point gold medal talent to 16-point gold medal talent. Now also applies to Mutilate.
  • Improved Poisons: Now also grants a large chance for Poisons not to consume charges when triggered. We want Assassination to be a Poison-focused playstyle, so this helps their Poisons last much longer without needing to be reapplied.
  • Vigor: Now a 2-point talent on row 5 instead of the 31-point gold medal talent. Same total effect.
  • Mutilate: (New 21-point gold medal talent.) This 60 Energy Combo ability strikes with both hands as weapon damage from each weapon, but both must be daggers. This damage is increased against Poisoned targets and awards 2 Combo Points. Each hand has a chance to trigger various procs.
  • Improved Kidney Shot: The increased damage from this talent now applies only to your own attacks and Poisons.
  • Seal Fate: No longer requires Cold Blood as a pre-requisite. Note that Mutilate will trigger this exactly once if either or both hands generates a critical strike.
  • Venom: New 31-point gold medal talent. This new 25 Energy Finisher ability grants 30% increased damage to your Poisons and 10% increased chance to apply Poisons. Duration determined by number of Combo Points spent. Our expectation is that Assassination focuses its finishers on maintaining Venom and Slice and Dice, and damaging finishers like Rupture and Eviscerate are a lower priority. Other Rogue builds would put more emphasis on those damaging Finishers.

Combat

  • Improved Eviscerate: Moved to row 1 from Assassination . Damage bonus increased.
  • Puncturing Wounds: (Formerly Improved Backstab.) Now also increased Mutilate damage but a lesser percentage, and gives Backstab a chance to grant an additional Combo Point.
  • Deflection: Now grants twice as much Parry chance per point.
  • Precision: Now increases chance to hit with all spells and attacks, including Poisons, instead of just melee weapon attacks.
  • Endurance: Now reduces Sprint and Evasion cooldown by a percentage, resulting in a larger total reduction for both.
  • Flawless Execution: New 16-point gold medal talent. Reduces the Energy cost of Eviscerate by 10.
  • Dual Wield Specialization: Increase to off-hand damage reduced.
  • Hack and Slash: This new row 5 talent combines the benefits of the removed talents Dagger Specialization, Mace Specialization, Sword Specialization, and Fist Weapon Specialization, and also adds a bonus for Axes. Axes gain the same benefit as Swords, a chance to make an extra attack. The bonus for Maces causes attacks to ignore some of the target’s armor, rather than provide a chance to Stun.
  • Weapon Expertise: (Redesigned.) Now reduces the chance for a target to Dodge or Parry your attacks.
  • Aggression: Now also increases Backstab damage. We wanted the Combat specialization to support a Backstab-oriented build as well as a Sinister Strike-oriented build. So, this and several other talents gained more Backstab support.
Removed talents: Dagger Specializaton, Mace Specialization, Sword Specialization, Fist Weapon Specialization have all been subsumed into the new talent Hack and Slash.

Subtlety

  • Camouflage: Moved from row 2 up to row 1.
  • Master of Deception: Reduced from 5 talent points to 3 talent points for the same effect. The tooltip has been clarified to state the exact impact of the improvement to Stealth.
  • Opportunity: Now also affects Mutilate.
  • Setup: Chance to trigger increased so that 3 points grants 100% chance.
  • Dirty Tricks: Formerly Improved Sap. Moved from row 4 up to row 2. (Redesigned.) Sap never breaks Stealth now baseline. Instead, this talent reduces the Energy cost of Sap and Blind by a substantial amount.
  • Improved Ambush: Moved from row 3 to row 2.
  • Initiative: Chance for this to activate increased so that it has a 100% chance with 3 talent points.
  • Ghostly Strike: Percentage damage done increased while a Dagger is equipped instead of another weapon.
  • Improved Distract: (New row 3 talent.) Increases the radius of effect of your Distract, and Distracted enemies now suffer an increased penalty to their Stealth detection.
  • Heightened Senses: Moved from row 5 up to row 4. Tooltip clarified to describe the exact effect of the increased Stealth detection.
  • Premeditation: Moved from 31-point gold medal talent to 16-point gold medal talent. Duration increased to 20 seconds.
  • Serrated Blades: Now ignores a specific percentage of your target’s armor, instead of a flat value—rising per level.
  • Dirty Deeds: Now also allows Garrote to be used when not behind your target.
  • Hemorrhage: Percentage damage done increased while a Dagger is equipped instead of another weapon. Now also increases your Rupture damage to the target for 15 seconds.
  • Quietus: (New row 6 talent.) Pre-requisite Dirty Deeds. Your Sinister Strike, Ghostly Strike, and Hemorrhage abilities cause more damage to targets below 35% health.
    We wanted the Subtlety tree to support playstyles with both Sinister Strike and Backstab, so this talent supports the Sinister Strike oriented build.
  • Cutthroat: (New row 6 talent.) Your Backstab has a chance to cause your next Ambush to not require Stealth.
    This talent supports the Backstab oriented build as well as creating an exciting alternate flow where Ambush can be used during combat.
  • Thousand Cuts: New 31-point gold medal talent. Each time Rupture deals damage, the Energy cost of your next Hemorrhage or Backstab ability is reduced by 3 Energy, stacking up to 5 times.
Removed talents: Sleight of Hand, Deadliness.
Rogues remain the masters of Stealth, with unique abilities useable from Stealth like Pickpocket, Distract, Sap, and Garrote. They alone have access to Poisons and can now use them alongside temporary weapon enchantments. However, different varieties of Rogues specialize in different weapons and tactics. Assassination specializes in daggers and buffing themselves with Finishing moves.  Combat and Subtlety have support for all weapon types, with Combat focusing on hard hitting direct damage and little bit of cleave damage with Sweeping Strikes, and Subtlety focusing on combat tricks and Bleeds. Whichever specialization they choose, Rogues are welcome in any party or raid for their Stealth and control abilities, as well as the highest potential single-target melee damage in the game.

Warlock: Power at Any Price


Warlocks bend forbidden powers to their will, turning every resource—from lingering afflictions to bound demons—into another means of defeating their enemies. These updates broaden how they manage those powers and create new connections among their spells, pets, and specialized tools.

Baseline Abilities

  • Curse of Agony and Curse of Doom are now Banes. Only one Bane can be active per Warlock on a single target. All effects that interacted with Curses now also interact with Banes.
  • Curse of the Elements now applies to all magic damage.
  • Curse of Shadows removed.
  • Firestone and Spellstone now apply Weapon Imbues, that can be stacked with other temporary enchantments like Wizard Oil. Firestone grants increased Fire damage and critical strike chance. Spellstone grants increased Shadow damage and spell haste.
  • Life Tap now scales with Spirit, and the amount of Mana from Spirit is correctly stated in its tooltip.
  • Drain Soul now has a progressive chance per tick to grant a Soul Shard (chance increases each time it doesn't happen, until guaranteed).
  • Pets now scale from their summoner’s stats.

Talents

Affliction

  • Convection: Now also reduces the Mana cost of Lava Burst.
  • Concussion: No longer applies to Frost Shock or Flame Shock.
  • Reverberation: Moved from row 3 up to row 2.
  • Call of Flame: Now also increases the damage done by Flame Shock, Fire Nova, and Lava Burst.
  • Elemental Devastation: Moved from row 4 up to row 2. This talent is intended primarily as a reason to entice Enhancement Shaman into spending points on Elemental talents, and so was made more accessible.
  • Elemental Focus: Chance to trigger reduced when casting low rank spells.
  • Elemental Alacrity: (Formerly Lightning Mastery.) Moved from row 6 up to row 3. Now requires only 3 points for maximum rank and reduces the cast time of Lightning Bolt and Chain Lightning by only 0.5 seconds at max rank but also reduces the cast time of Lava Burst. This talent was both very deep in the tree previously, making it unavailable to Shaman leveling up, and was twice as strong as similar talents with other classes, causing a spell power scaling problem. To account for this, its potency was reduced and it was moved much earlier in the tree.
  • Improved Fire Nova: (Formerly Improved Fire Totems. Redesigned.) Now increases Fire Nova’s damage and reduces its cooldown.
  • Eye of the Storm: (Redesigned.) This talent now grants resistance against spell pushback from damage while casting Lightning Bolt, Chain Lightning, and Lava Burst.Formerly it was only effective after being hit with a critical strike. This talent was previously only really useful in PvP. It is now useful broadly in the game.
  • Call of Thunder: Moved from the row 3 down to row 4, and now has Elemental Alacrity as a pre-requisite. This talent is now the 16-point gold medal talent, granting 3% increased critical strike chance to Lighting Bolt and Chain Lightning.
  • Elemental Reach: Now also increases the range of Fire Nova and Lava Burst by up to 6 yards and increases the range of Flame Shock by up to 15 yards.
  • Lighting Overload: This new row 5 talent grants a chance for every cast of Lightning Bolt or Chain Lighting to instantly cast a second copy of that spell at no Mana cost but for half damage and no threat.
  • Earthbound: This new 21-point gold medal talent causes Earthbind Totem to instantly immobilize nearby targets for 5 seconds when cast.
  • Elemental Fury: Moved from row 5 down to row 6 and requires Call of Thunder as a pre-requisite.
  • Lava Burst: This new 31-point gold medal talent grants the Lava Burst spell. This 2.5 second cast spell deals Fire damage to a target, increased by 20% if the target is afflicted by your Flame Shock. 10 second cooldown.
Removed talents: None.

Demonology

  • Improved Imp: No longer effects its Blood Pact spell.
  • Demonic Embrace: No longer reduces your Spirit.
  • Unholy Power: Moved from row 4 up to row 1 and damage bonus to pets decreased.
  • Improved Health Funnel: Moved from row 2 up to row 1. Health transfer bonus increased and now also reduces the threat your Health Funnel generates by up to 100%. Also allows Health Funnel to be used regardless of your demon's health.
  • Demonic Aegis: (New row 2 talent.) Increases the effectiveness of your Demon Skin and Demon Armor spells by up to 30%.
  • Fel Vitality: (New row 2 talent.) Increases the maximum health and Mana of your Imp, Voidwalker, Succubus, Incubus, and Felhunter by up to 15% and increases your maximum Mana by up to 15%.
  • Demonic Energies: (New row 2 talent.) You heal your pet for up to 15% of all spell damage you deal. When you gain Mana from Life Tap, your summoned demon gains up to 100% of the mana you gain.
  • Fel Domination: Now the 16-point gold medal talent and requires Master Summoner as a pre-requisite.
  • Master Summoner moved from row 4 up to row 3.
  • Demonic Sacrifice: (Redesigned) Now the 11-point gold medal talent. Sacrifice effects last 2 hours and effects from each sacrifice have shifted around: Imp increases Shadow damage, Voidwalker restores mana, Succubus/Incubus increase fire damage and Felhunter restores Health.
  • Decimation: (New row 4 talent.) Reduces the cooldown of your Soul Fire spell by up to 90%. When you cast Shadow Bolt or Searing Pain on an enemy below 35% health, they deal increased damage and your Soul Fire spell for the next 10 seconds has its cast time reduced by up to 40% and costs no Soul Shards.
  • Demonic Brand: (New row 4 talent.) Your Searing Pain generates less threat and brands the target, causing your pet’s next 2 attacks to deal Fire or Shadow damage depending on the pet. If using Shadow damage, it is high threat.
    We made a recent change to the threat component, so a non-tanking pet like the Warlock’s Imp does not gain extra threat, but a tanking-oriented pet like the Voidwalker does.
  • Soul Link moved from row 7 up to row 5.
  • Improved Felhunter: (New row 5 talent. Increase the Attack Power reduction of your Felhunter’s Tainted Blood, the healing of its Devour Magic, and the detection level of its Paranoia by 10% and reduce the cooldown of its Spell Lock by 2 seconds.
  • Soul Link: Now the 21-point gold medal talent instead of the 31-point.
  • Demonic Knowledge: (New row 5 talent. Increases your spell damage and your Demon pet’s spell damage by up to 33% of your level while you have a summoned Demon pet active.
  • Master Demonologist redesigned: Bonuses provided by each pet changed. Imp increases Fire damage done, Voidwalker reduces Physical damage taken, Succubus/Incubus Increases Shadow damage done and Felhunter reduces Magic damage taken.
  • Demonic Pact: New 31-point gold medal talent. Requires Soul Link. Your Demonic Sacrifice effect is no longer cancelled by summoning a different pet. Resummoning the sacrificed pet will still cancel the effect.
    This exciting new talent allows Warlocks for the first time to benefit from Demonic Sacrifice and Master Demonologist at the same time. How a Demonologist Warlock decides to stack these two effects will have a large impact on their combat abilities.
Removed talents: Improved Healthstone, Fel Intellect, Fel Stamina, Improved Subjugate Demon, Improved Firestone, Improved Spellstone.

Destruction

  • Destructive Reach: Moved from row 4 up to row 1. Now applies to all damaging spells, not just Destruction spells. This talent now benefits every Warlock specialization and is in easy reach of them all in the first row.
  • Improved Shadow Bolt: Now only applies to your own Shadow damage but no longer has charges that can be consumed.
  • Bane: Moved from row 2 to row 1. Now also applies to Incinerate.
  • Cataclysm: Moved from row 1 down to row 2 and now reduces mana cost of your Destruction spells by up to 10%.
  • Molten Skin: (New row 2 talent) Reduces all damage taken by up to 10%.
  • Aftermath: (Redesigned) Increases the initial damage of your Immolate spell by up to 50% and your Conflagrate spell has up to 100% chance to Daze the target, reducing the target’s movement speed by 50% for 5 seconds.
  • Ruin moved from row 5 up to row 3 and is now a 5-point talent for the same effect. This makes it more accessible for Demonology and hybrid builds that would benefit.
  • Agonizing Flames: (Formerly Improved Searing Pain) Now only 3 talent points. Increases the damage of all of your Destruction spells in addition to increasing the critical strike chance of your Searing Pain.
  • Conflagrate: Moved from row 7 up to row 4. Now the 16-point gold medal talent.
  • Intensity: Now a 3-point talent instead of 2 and gives resistance to cast time loss from taking damage to all Destruction spells, not just Rain of Fire, Hellfire, and Soulfire.
  • Pyroclasm: Wording improved to make effect more clear.
  • Fire and Brimstone: (New row 5 talent) Requires Conflagrate. Increases the critical strike chance of your Conflagrate.
  • Bane of Havoc: (New 21-point gold medal talent) Afflicts the target for 5 minutes causing 15% of all damage done by the Warlock to other targets to also be dealt to the cursed target. Limited to 1 target and only one Bane per Warlock can be active on any one target.
  • Shadow and Flame: New row 6 talent.) Hitting an enemy with Conflagrate increases all Shadow damage you deal for 20 seconds and hitting an enemy with Shadowburn increases all Fire damage you deal for 20 seconds. In addition, Conflagrate has up to 100% chance to not consume Immolate and Shadowburn has up to 100% chance to instantly refund a Soul Shard.
  • Incinerate: (New 31-point gold medal talent.) Requires Bane of Havoc. Deals Fire damage to your target and an additional 25% damage if the target is afflicted by Immolate. 2.5 seconds cast, 30-yard range.
Removed talents:  Improved Firebolt, Improved Lash of Pain, Devastation, Improved Immolate, Emberstorm.

Warlocks are gaining new exciting combat options for WoW: Forever. With Affliction, they can concentrate on damage-over-time and draining effects, now with full viability from dealing critical strikes and competitive damage, and with the ability to sustain their own health via powerful health draining effects. With Demonology, they can specialize in empowering themselves and their pet in all new ways with Demonic Brand, Demonic Knowledge, and Demonic Pact, keeping foes focused on their pet while they decimate the enemy with Soul Fire. And with Destruction, they can now mix powerful Shadowburns and Conflagrates with the new Incinerate spell, and the new Bane of Havoc allowing them to continue damage on a primary target while dealing with lesser foes. Warlocks are still physically weak themselves, depending on their demon pets for protection, but they now do damage to compete with any other spellcaster, with three completely different styles to conduct that competition.
Whether striking from the shadows or wielding forbidden power, Rogues and Warlocks offer distinct ways to approach every encounter. Explore their updated talents, experiment with new combinations, and find the tactics that best suit your path through World of Warcraft: Forever.

title.en: SD Skyborne Models and Druid Forms Arriving in Early 2027
title.es: Modelos SD Skyborne y formas Druidaas que llegarán a principios de 2027

summary.en: SD Skyborne Models and Druid Forms Arriving in Early 2027...
summary.es: Modelos SD Skyborne y formas Druidaas que llegarán a principios de 2027...

contentHtml:
Blizzard has announced that SD Skyborne Models and Druid forms will release in early 2027!

SD Skyborne models have asked for by the Classic community and they’re coming next year! In addition, Blizzard will be updating the HD Druid Forms to have them fit better in WoW: Forever.
Blizzard
View Original
The World of Warcraft development team began our journey into World of Warcraft: Forever with ambitions that grew and evolved over time. Our aim has always been to uphold the original WoW era aesthetic, while giving players more choice in how they experience Azeroth.

Over the course of development, we have been aligning on the right range of fidelity and what feels like it belongs in the WoW: Forever world and what does not. The team has learned much in the process, and that will continue to strengthen more with future content.

Along the way, there were some ideas the team wanted to explore that ultimately didn’t quite meet the consistency and cohesion we are aiming for. To align with our goals better, we are taking aim at updating some of those visuals for the future. Here is one example of how we are revisiting the High Definition (HD) Skyborne Druid forms.

We removed a bit of the softness, added more detailed fur textures, and adjusted the color saturation. The Skyborne are from an exotic environment, and their Druid forms reflect that, but we don't want that to be dissonant with the visual language of other creatures in the world.

Skyborne Standard Definition (SD) Player Character Update

In choosing to offer an SD or HD toggle for player characters, we focused on the pre-existing races from original World of Warcraft since many people have an attachment to those models. However, we have heard feedback that the HD Skyborne can be jarring by contrast when placed in the same world as the SD models and world, and we agree.

So, for those of us that prefer the look of SD models and want more choice, Skyborne player characters (and yes SD Druid forms) are in development and arriving early 2027. We look forward to sharing more information closer to that date. For now, here is an early work in progress image.
This is just the start of our journey, and the whole team is thrilled with the reception for World of Warcraft: Forever. As we continue refining this vision together, we look forward to what lies ahead—for the Horde! For the Alliance! Forever!

title.en: New Battleground Preview in World of Warcraft: Forever - Battle for the Darkspear Islands
title.es: Nueva vista previa del campo de batalla en World of Warcraft: Forever - Battle for the Darkspear Islands

summary.en: New Battleground Preview in World of Warcraft: Forever - Battle for the Darkspear Islands...
summary.es: Nueva vista previa del campo de batalla en World of Warcraft: Forever - Battle for the Darkspear Islands...

contentHtml:
Blizzard has released a preview of the new Battle for the Darkspear Islands battleground in World of Warcraft: Forever!

This Battleground is a brand new 15v15 battleground off the coast of Dustwallow Marsh for players level 30 or higher. Each team is tasked with capturing points and holding them to get 2,000 score first.
Blizzard
View Original
Off the coast of Dustwallow Marsh lies the Darkspear Islands, where a new battle is taking shape. In this 15v15 battleground, the Darkspear Raiders and Theramore Expeditionary Force clash for control of strategic footholds, a central flag, and the rewards waiting for those willing to fight for their faction.
Type of Map: 15v15 Capture Point with a Flag Capture Battleground  
Location: Off the Shores of Dustwallow Marsh 
Player Levels: 30-60 
Victory Condition: First team to 2000 Points

Your Mission: Capture and Hold

   
Teams earn points by controlling four capture points across the Darkspear Islands. The more capture points your team controls, the quicker your team accrues points. A flag waits in the middle of the map, giving both teams another objective to fight over. Grab it, bring it to one of the bases your team has captured, and earn more points for your side. The first team to earn 2000 points wins!
  

Queue Up for Battle


You can queue for the battleground in a couple of ways. Visit a battlemaster located in any major capital city or in the Barrens (Kalimdor) seek out the Darkspear Raiders base (Horde) at the Merchant Coast or Theramore Expeditionary Force (Alliance) base located at Northwatch, where a portal will take you into the battle.

These bases also include vendors with reputation rewards you can acquire as you increase your standing with the Darkspear Raiders or Theramore Expeditionary Force. In these areas, you can also pick up quests for the battleground.

Earn Battleground Rewards


There is a reputation track for each faction for the Battleground: Darkspear Raiders and Theramore Expeditionary Force. They have gear and consumables that you can purchase including trinkets, rings, cloaks, weapons, armor pieces when hitting different reputation thresholds. And of course, there are quests for the Battleground. Turn in for Marks of Honor for reputation quests and unlock a short questline at Exalted to earn the faction's exclusive tabard.
Rally your allies, queue up for battle, and fight to secure the Darkspear Islands for your faction in WoW: Forever.j

author: Wowhead Staff

title.en: Myth Track Gear Awarded from Delve Labyrinths in Patch 12.1.5
title.es: Myth Track Gear otorgado por Delve Labyrinths en el parche 12.1.5

summary.en: Myth Track Gear Awarded from Delve Labyrinths in Patch 12.1.5...
summary.es: Myth Track Gear otorgado por Delve Labyrinths en el parche 12.1.5...

contentHtml:
The Labyrinth of Kindo'jan releases on October 13th with Patch 12.1.5, and players can get a piece of Myth track gear from Labyrinths!

After you unlock Labyrinths in Patch 12.1.5 and you complete the introduction quest, a new NPC, Wah'du, will be at the entrance and have a quest for you. This quest will task you with going to a chamber in the Labyrinth and finishing the objective there on Tier 8 or above.

Completing the quest will earn you one Mythical Soul Fragment and 2,000 Undercoin. On PTR, Wah'du will then have another similar quest for you, but for another zone, but it's likely that on live servers these quests are Weekly Gated. Once you complete 3 quests and have 3 Mythical Soul Fragments, you can combine them to get a Myth 1/6 piece of gear. The best part is that you can choose the slot that you want it for!

 


If you're looking for a piece of Myth track gear, this is a great way to spend some Myth crests once Patch 12.1.5 comes out.

summary.en: How PvP Progression Works in World of Warcraft: Forever...
summary.es: Cómo funciona la progresión PvP en World of Warcraft: Forever...

contentHtml:
Blizzard has provided details on how PvP progression works in World of Warcraft: Forever!

Some of the biggest highlights include:
  • The Honor currency returns with increased Honor gains in holiday week Battlegrounds.
  • Honor has been reworked, so Alterac Valley isn't always the best for Honor efficiency.
  • Rank Points come from PvP activities and will advance through familiar PvP Ranks. There's a weekly cap.
  • Honor will be used to purchase PvP gear: one blue-quality and one epic-quality.
  • Epic quality will need the blue-version and an item that requires a rank requirement.
  • New items fill in specialization gaps -- Shaman will have healer, melee and caster PvP gear sets.
  • PvP Seasons will have weekly tasks to complete granting Honor and Rank Points with 3 tasks earning a Legacy Point.
Blizzard
View Original
Whether you’re charging into battlegrounds with your faction or setting your sights on long-term PvP (Player vs. Player) goals, World of Warcraft: Forever brings a refreshed sense of purpose to every match-up. This approach gives players more reasons to take part throughout the season while preserving the spirit of competition that defined PvP in the original World of Warcraft.

Approachable and Familiar

When reimagining the PvP system, we wanted to keep the design pillar of “Approachable and Familiar” firmly in view: simplifying the original Honor System while staying true to its roots.

Progressing Through the Ranks

In World of Warcraft: Forever, PvP progression has two parts: Honor and Rank Points.

Honor

Honor is a currency players earn through taking part in PvP content. This includes defeating other players, completing battlegrounds, and finishing relevant PvP quests. Players also earn increased Honor in highlighted battlegrounds during their holiday weeks.

As part of these updates, we reviewed Honor gains across battlegrounds so acquisition rates are more consistent across the board. We want players to enjoy the full range of battleground maps without feeling compelled to choose Alterac Valley solely for Honor efficiency.

Rank Points

Rank Points come from PvP activities such as battlegrounds and relevant PvP quests, with holiday-week battlegrounds offering an additional boost. As players earn Rank Points, they advance through familiar PvP ranks from original World of Warcraft, working toward the ultimate titles of High Warlord for the Horde or Grand Marshal for the Alliance. Ranks have a weekly cap, retaining the foundation of the original system while making the journey more accessible.

Gearing Up for Battle

Honor can be used to purchase two sets of PvP gear: one blue-quality set and one epic-quality set. The epic set requires the blue piece plus an Emboldened Seal to upgrade it, and Emboldened Seals have rank requirements players must reach before purchasing. There are also new and reworked items to fill gaps for specializations that were previously missing options. For example, Shaman now have healer, melee, and caster PvP gear sets they can acquire.

Below are the rank requirements for PvP item rewards:

Rank 1 - Tabard
Rank 2 - PvP Trinket
Rank 3 - Cloaks
Rank 4 - Necklace
Rank 5 - Combat Potions
Rank 6 - Tabard
Rank 7 - Battle Standard
Rank 8 - Epic Bracers/Epic Belt Upgrade Token
Rank 9 - Epic Boots Upgrade Token
Rank 10 - Epic Gloves Upgrade Token
Rank 11 - Mounts
Rank 12 - Epic Legs/Epic Shoulders Upgrade Token
Rank 13 - Epic Chest/Epic Helm Upgrade Token
Rank 14 - Epic Weapons

To view your progress, you can open your Character Pane (Hotkey-C) then select the Player vs. Player tab on the right side of the interface. It will show you your rank, your current Rank Points, and what rewards are available for purchase based on your rank.

PvP Seasons

During a PvP season, players can progress through the ranks and earn Honor. Each season also includes a journey with weekly tasks to complete. Successfully completing those tasks grants Honor and Rank Points, and three tasks each season also grant a Legacy Point. Completing these tasks is part of the seasonal journey, and because they are tied to the Legacy System, they remain available to complete in future seasons.
With more ways to make progress each week and meaningful goals to pursue throughout the season, PvP in World of Warcraft: Forever gives players a clear path to jump in, compete, and keep building toward what comes next.

title.en: WoW: Forever Warrior Deep Dive - What Changed, and What is Still Needed?
title.es: WoW: Forever Guerrero Deep Dive - ¿Qué ha cambiado y qué se necesita todavía?

summary.es: WoW: Forever Guerrero Deep Dive - ¿Qué ha cambiado y qué se necesita todavía?...

contentHtml:
Warriors are quite possibly one of the most, if not the most, iconic classes in Classic. WoW: Forever brings quite a few adjustments to this class, so our Fury class expert Babyhoof dives into everything Warrior - the good, the bad, and what needs to change.
Ever since its rework in the Original Patch 1.6, Warrior DPS has only gotten better and better, both in its perceived viability as well as its power. By the end of the Original run of Vanilla, Warrior had clawed its way into being a respectable DPS class, and by the time Classic rolled around in 2019 was considered the best DPS in the game. The gap between DPS Warrior and every other class was immense, and was incomparable to any other gap between DPS specs across the history of the game, with the possible exception of early Death Knights in Naxxramas during WotLK Classic. As such, Warrior was fully expected to receive heavy changes heading into Forever, and while some of the removals and additions we have seen feel both expected and understandable, others only seem to invite more questions.

Rage and all its friends

To address the Devilsaur in the room, Rage Normalization was, in my opinion, a change that was much needed. Rage normalization refers to the change made in Cataclysm where instead of Rage being generated with a formula based on damage dealt with auto attacks, Rage is instead generated with a flat amount based on swing speed, with a bonus amount generated with Critical Strikes. Non normalized Rage was by far one of the most prominent issues with DPS Warrior; gear not only increased your damage outright, but also scaled the amount you could press abilities, leading to a situation where the gap between gear levels was far higher than it initially seemed. This gap could be felt even when leveling; Getting a new weapon not only sped you up simply by the fact that you had a better weapon in the first place, but your rage generation would be increased by a significant amount as well.

Rage became a much bigger issue with Dual Wielding, however. Due to a major bug with the way the game recognized attack tables, queuing an "on next attack" ability such as Heroic Strike or Cleave would remove the Dual Wield miss penalty from your offhand while the ability was queued. This meant that a major disadvantage of Dual Wielding, the added chance to miss with your auto attacks, was completely removed, and in raiding content meant that your rage generation was vastly above what it should be. Instead of these abilities becoming a way to dump extra rage, they became a much more common part of your rotation because simply pressing them had a good chance of your off-hand generating more rage than you would spend on the ability. Once again the problem became even worse with gear, and at end game you could simply ignore your rage bar for a large part of the fight unless you got a streak of unlucky dodges. This bug persisted all the way through until Heroic Strike was reworked in Cataclysm, and has finally been fixed in Forever, although we have received the Furious Precision talent to compensate for its loss.

The initial variant of Rage Normalization we received, however, had several significant issues. The first, and most important issue, was that it simply did not generate enough rage. The base formula for Rage generation is expressed as a simple formula, as displayed below

base  = 3.46 x weaponSpeed x handMultiplier          (off-hand: half)
swing = base x 1.3 for a two-hander, else base
Credit to The Forever Warrior Github

With this amount of Rage generation, Warrior struggled to keep its abilities on cooldown, and the relatively fluid and active play style it enjoyed before was almost completely removed. Not only did your abilities cost a large amount of rage, you generated it relatively slowly, and your stats were far worse than before - the removal of easy access to Weapon Skill through racials and easily accessible items such as Edgemaster's Handguards meant that you needed more hit to achieve your soft cap than before. Most notably, the rage scaling with gear the spec enjoyed had almost completely vanished - critical strikes in the initial build of Forever did not give extra rage, making the only way to generate more rage to stack Hit %, a design that ran antithetical to one of our talents that already gave us hit on our offhand.

This rework was met with no small degree of outcry - While DPS Warrior had needed a nerf from its 1.12 iteration, this had been far too brutal. The low rate of Rage generation would cause the spec to be incredibly slow in end game content, and go from being a spec with one of the more active play styles to one where you would be expected to potentially press no buttons for ten or more seconds. Blizzard quickly announced changes two weeks after the Beta went live, however - adding a 75% additional rage modifier to critical strikes, before increasing it to 100% the same day due to their internal metrics being influenced by a bug with one of the talents.


An image comparison (Credit to Marrows Compendium) of how our rage generation compares between the 3 versions of Forever and Classic.

This change finally put Warrior rage generation where it should be - enough to press your main rotational abilities on cooldown, not enough to spend the whole fight spending Rage on Heroic Strike, but with a way to gradually increase our ability to press more buttons through gathering Critical Strike, an attribute we must balance with the rest of our gear. Blizzard will need to pay close attention, however, and adjust both our base rage gain and the amount we generate from Critical Strikes in case we are either generating far too much or, in all likelihood, still generating not quite enough.

Talents and Abilities

When compared to some other classes and specs, DPS Warrior gained very few new toys to play with in WoW Forever. Victory Rush is possibly the biggest of these additions, but is mostly a leveling bonus; landing killing blows in end game content is rare, and the spell doesn't hit hard enough to consider it a big loss to be unable to proc it reliably anyway. The other major new addition is in the form of Tactical Mastery now having a baseline component, letting us conserve a small amount of rage when changing stances without a talent point investment.

The Fury Tree in particular is a stark reminder that the class has been significantly pruned down; several of the new talents are added only to compensate for removals of features we had before. Furious Precision only exists to serve as a replacement for the Heroic Strike Queuing mechanic, and the minor amount of damage added to Bloodthirst barely compensates for several of our key buffs in Battle Shout and Blessing of Might having a large chunk of their attack power removed. Even one of our core talents in Flurry had its max attack speed reduced from 30% to 25%.

The Arms Tree has a few new toys to play with, but apart from one major new talent that does add some much needed rage efficiency, the changes are very small. Bloodthrill is admittedly a strong new addition to our arsenal, being a proc that allows us to use one of our most rage efficient spells in Overpower that would normally not see a huge amount of use, also allowing us to feel as if our Improved Overpower has more impact. Everything else that was added, however, feels quite underwhelming. Spearing Strike is relegated to either incredibly niche PvP usages, or a long cooldown spell that is weak against all but a few enemy types. Weaponmaster is simply a condensing of the original different weapon type talents, with an added PvE bonus for maces. Improved Slam would be a fantastic new addition, if the baseline ability Slam hadn't been slapped with a quite frankly brutal 18 second cooldown.

Fury also maintains a baffling conditional on its core stance; Berserker Stance continues to increase our damage taken by a quite frankly unreasonable 10%. The "melee tax", a concept where melee specs inevitably take more damage from abilities due to having a smaller area in which they can deal damage but in return are given either increased survivability or are able to deal more damage in return appears to apply to some specs and not others in WoW Forever - why must we continue to pay this more heavily than any other spec? Retribution Paladins have the ability to become immune and self heal, Enhancement Shamans can self heal, Survival Hunters can go out to range. The closest comparisons are Rogues and Feral Druids, but both specs do not have an increased damage taken modifier. Is the intention that we are being made to compensate for our higher armour? If so, why does this damage taken increase translate to Magical Damage as well? If the intention is to punish us for being in a higher DPS stance, why is there not an effort to enable playing in Battle Stance more; Arms Warriors must be in it in order to apply and use their Rend and Overpower abilities, but Fury must suffer in Berserker Stance the whole time. While we have Death Wish active the situation is even worse, totaling a quite miserable 15% total damage taken increase, a not insignificant number. For reference, this is roughly the % increase Fury Warrior was ahead of other specs in Single Target fights during Blackwing Lair in the recent Classic Anniversary Run, and that was considered an unacceptable advantage to the point of being ridiculed..

Stances in general are a topic I would not be opposed to being expanded upon. Stances have been a core part of a Warriors identity for the majority of WoWs lifetime, and is a fantastic RPG-esque mechanic that lets us feel as if our choice of stance has an impact on how you are playing. At least, this is how its supposed to work in theory. Currently, each stance is hard assigned to a certain spec - Arms is forced into Battle Stance because they cannot cast core parts of their rotation in Rend and Overpower without it, Protection must stay in Defensive Stance in order to use the majority of their abilities as well as deal additional threat, and Fury is locked into Berserker Stance in order to use one of their two rotational abilities, Whirlwind. If the goal of these designs is to make players swap between stances more often, then the paltry 25 rage you get to keep when swapping feels like far too little - Arms Warriors get enough to cast Whirlwind and nothing more, while Fury cannot swap to Battle Stance to cast Overpower during gaps in their rotation without risking not being able to cast their other core abilities. To make matters worse, Battle Stance has no positive effects associated with it, making spending time in the stance feel as if you are powered down when compared to the small critical strike increase of Berserker Stance. If the goal is to make swapping between stances the core playstyle, then why is the amount of Rage we get to keep not increased? Tactical Mastery having a baseline component now seems really good, until you realize that the talent that it used to encompass in Improved Tactical Mastery now gives less per point, meaning that we are conserving exactly the same amount of rage! This feels like a much unneeded adjustment, and one that could easily be changed to let a more satisfying play style where you enjoy switching between stances take root, instead of dreading having to swap. If the goal is to preserve stance to spec identity, then adding a bonus to Battle Stance somehow makes sense - Arms seems like it will suffer in Rage generation when compared to Fury, so I would propose adding a talent in place of the underwhelming Spearing Strike that gives you a chance to proc extra Rage while in Battle Stance. Now, each of the stances has a modifier of some form, and you don't feel overly punished for spending time in any of them situationally.

Finally, one of our spec defining abilities is the source of much discussion and controversy, especially surrounding its cooldown. Recklessness is an iconic Warrior ability, but one that seems to have been intentionally ignored by the developers due to its power, remaining at a staggering 30 minute cooldown. If the class having a shorter cooldown would make it unbalanced, why is the power of the ability not being lowered? If the intention is to preserve the fantasy of being able to use this ability and become very powerful for a short duration of time a few times every night, surely reducing the effects and cooldown by 50% would make it far more satisfying. If the ability existing at all is causing issues balancing the class in end game content, I would much prefer it to be simply removed and power given to the class in other ways. A good Recklessness feels fantastic, yes, but this is always balanced out by pressing the ability and promptly either having a string of terrible RNG with ability dodges, being rage starved (a much more likely occurrence in WoW Forever), or simply getting chosen for a mechanic that requires you to disengage from the boss. The latter is not an argument for being told to not press it on a boss, either; the moment you start disqualifying entire encounters from being viable fights to use your spec defining ability on, the argument for it being a tool to balance around sheds all viability.

All of these facts come together to paint a somewhat saddening picture; DPS Warriors aren't allowed to get anything new without losing something we already had. Where as other classes have received large overhauls and fancy reworks, DPS Warriors have merely been given consolation prizes that are simply equal or worse to what we already had, and expected to be happy with it.

What do we actually need?

Warrior does not need a return to its 2019 state. Even the most fervent Warrior player can agree that that version of the class was overtuned and ridiculous. The class doesn't need a lot to feel better, however, and adding too much could run the risk of not being able to preserve a more "Classic" feel.

The first and most important change is a way to reduce our rage expenditure in cleave. A stated goal of the Warrior class fantasy is the ability to "sustain cleave like no other class can", and yet our primary damage dealer in these scenarios, the aptly named Cleave spell, costs a significant amount of rage while also preventing your mainhand swing from generating any. This raises the rage cost on the ability far beyond its base cost - if you get a critical strike on your cleave ability it still counts as an ability swing, and does not generate extra rage. This means that our rage consumption in cleave is very high - we can either give up major single target damage by delaying our Bloodthirst ability, or accept that our rage generation isn't high enough to actually be able to perform the role that the developers have set out to make us able to do. There are several easy solutions to this - Reducing the rage cost of the spell itself, giving a refund when 2 targets are hit, or even giving a talent that increases the amount of targets hit by 1, similar to the Wrath of the Lich King glyph. However, my personal request for the ability would be for swings made while Cleave and Heroic Strike are queued to still generate rage, even at a 50% penalty. This helps alleviate some of the high rage cost for committing to our damage profile, while still having a moderate cost to being able to perform AoE consistently and having satisfying gear scaling.

Another spell that needs modification to lessen the monotony is Sunder Armor. In Classic WoW, you could expect to have a fair number of Warriors in your raid, and applying and maintaining this debuff was a shared responsibility amongst a large number of players. In WoW Forever, however, raid sizes have significantly shrunk for most content - while 40 man raids, exist, the first tier of content has only a single 40 man boss, and the majority of raiding will be done in either 10 or 20 man environments. In these compositions, there is a good chance you will have no other Warriors raiding with you, depending on the perceived strength of the class, and this results in a situation where a Warrior must commit the opening 5 globals of every fight to applying a debuff, at a not insignificant rage cost. This debuff must also be maintained throughout the fight, again at a rage cost, and any time a new focus target appears, such as a new boss type mob within an encounter, this process must be repeated. No other class pays this much price for applying its utility - other Armor debuffs in Faerie Fire and Curse of Recklessness have both a longer duration, lower opportunity cost, and apply their full benefit instantly. I would like to see the stacks of this ability reduced to a maximum of 3, similar to later expansions, and a way to maintain the debuff at a reduced cost given.

Lingering Doubts

As it stands, Warrior looks fine in end game PvE; Numerically, that is. The class has lost its higher APM gameplay that was a core tenet of the Classic playstyle, has been forced into taking talents that give us removed features back, and seems to have been selected to receive a lot of the utility punishment that other specs have had removed. A lot of this ultimately will come down to how encounters are designed, and how they interact with our kit. Encounters with sustained two to three target cleave, Execute phases that require heavy burst damage, or encounters with light to medium incoming damage are all profiles that heavily support our playstyle and kit. If the encounter is focused mostly on single target, mass AoE, or the damage is too heavy, then Warrior seems to suffer from the perils of its design philosophy; balancing around abilities that are too long of a cooldown and too expensive both Rage and Opportunity cost wise means that DPS Warrior rests on a knifes edge of viability. Only time will tell how these boss fights are designed, and they could be a make or break for one of WoWs most iconic specs.
